facts.statement: Strong and colleagues named the genus Gavialimimus in 2020 based on an articulated skull and fragmentary postcrania found in the Ouled Abdoun Basin.
facts.quote: In 2020, Strong and colleagues named a new genus of plioplatecarpine mosasaur Gavialimimus based on the specimen MHNM.KHG.1231, an articulated skull and associated fragmentary postcrania found in the Ouled Abdoun Basin

facts.statement: Gavialimimus lived during the Maastrichtian stage in Morocco and possibly Angola.
facts.quote: Gavialimimus is an extinct genus of plioplatecarpine mosasaur from the Maastrichtian of Morocco and possibly Angola

facts.statement: A 4-meter long specimen of Gavialimimus was found in the stomach contents of a 6.5 to 7-meter long Prognathodon kianda in Angola.
facts.quote: In 2023, Polcyn, Schulp and Gonçalves described the gut contents of a 6.5 - 7 m long mosasaur specimen identified as Prognathodon kianda (MGUAN PA183) from Angola, which preserved three species of mosasaurs: a 4 m long specimen of Gavialimimus sp. (MGUAN PA183B)

facts.statement: Gut contents analysis suggests that Prognathodon kianda preferred to eat the heads of other mosasaurs, including Gavialimimus.
facts.quote: The size of Gavialimimus sp. was about 57% the size of P. kianda, and most of the gut contents of P. kianda were cranial material, suggesting that Prognathodon preferred to consume the head portion of other mosasaurs including relatively large taxa and its own kind

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that larger prognathodontine mosasaurs preyed upon Gavialimimus.
facts.quote: Some specimens suggest that larger prognathodontine mosasaurs preyed upon Gavialimimus

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Gavialimimus within the clade Selmasaurini, which also includes Goronyosaurus and Selmasaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2024 description of the Moroccan plioplatecarpine Khinjaria, Longrich et al. used phylogenetic analyses to recover it within a clade of non-plioplatecarpin plioplatecarpine mosasaurids. They named this clade—also containing Gavialimimus, Goronyosaurus and Selmasaurus—the Selmasaurini

facts.statement: Gavialimimus belongs to the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
Gavialimimus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
